name: Scala Functional Patterns
description: Enforces functional programming patterns in Scala including immutability, ADTs, and effect management.
content:
# Scala Functional Patterns Rules

- Prefer `val` over `var` — immutable bindings by default, mutable only when performance-critical and localized
- Use `case class` for data and `sealed trait` (or `enum` in Scala 3) for algebraic data types — enable exhaustive pattern matching
- Avoid `null` entirely — use `Option[T]` for optional values, `Either[E, A]` for operations that can fail
- Use `for` comprehensions to compose monadic operations — `Future`, `Option`, `Either`, `IO`
- Prefer pure functions — same input always produces same output, no side effects
- Push side effects to the edges — keep business logic pure, handle IO at the boundary
- Use type classes (`given`/`using` in Scala 3, `implicit` in Scala 2) for ad-hoc polymorphism
- Prefer `map`, `flatMap`, `filter`, `fold` over imperative loops — transform data, don't mutate it
- Use opaque types (Scala 3) or value classes to create zero-cost type-safe wrappers
- Use pattern matching with guards instead of if-else chains for complex branching
- Use `cats`, `zio`, or `fs2` for effect management — don't scatter raw `Future`s through business logic
- Avoid `Any`, `asInstanceOf`, and `isInstanceOf` — they bypass the type system and hide bugs
